text:
maya: Heads-up: we're getting requests to change burst behavior — customers want predictable bursts but we keep noisy-neighbor complaints. Proposal: bounded per-org burst credits + short smoothing window + dashboard visibility. Thoughts?

sam: Agree on visibility. We should show remaining burst credit in Console and expose via GET /v1/usage (include burst_tokens). Also add webhook for low-burst alerts so SEs can warn customers.

neha: How do we calculate credit? Fixed token-bucket per org with refill rate? Or dynamic based on commit? Need to avoid gaming (spikes just to get larger bucket).

jordan: Token-bucket + adaptive refill where refill_rate = max(static_rate, recent_1h_avg*alpha). Also flag if 1m spike > 10x baseline -> noisy neighbor alert. Use p50/p95 windows for sensitivity.

maya: Can we auto-route to cheaper model variant when hitting soft cap? e.g., model-xyz -> model-xyz-quantized or lower-seq model as fallback. That should reduce cost while keeping response acceptable.

eric: Yes but we must surface quality regressions. Make routing policy opt-in per org; default on for paid tiers, off for free. Also tie to eval sets so we can estimate expected delta.

sam: UX idea: Console toggle 'Enable soft-fallback during bursts' with tooltip explaining quality tradeoffs. Also show live widget: current_burst_tokens / max_tokens. Defaults: free tenants off, paid on? open to debate.

neha: Telemetry we need: per-tenant burst events, fallback events, latency/regression deltas, token cost delta. Also correlate with host-level telemetry (GPU utilization, contention) for noisy neighbor detection.

ops-bot: deploy:burst-metering v1 scheduled to canary at 22:00 UTC. /deploy 2200

jordan: Implementation note: enforcement path must be cheap. Prefer soft-throttle (delay + 429 with Retry-After) over heavy ingress checks. Also support quick queueing (100-500ms) for smoothing.

maya: Propose three-tier behavior: 1) soft smoothing (short delay 100-500ms) 2) fallback to cheaper model variant 3) hard reject when burst_tokens exhausted. Policy configurable per org/plan.

eric: Metrics to expose to customers: current_burst_tokens, refill_rate, soft_threshold, last_fallback_ts. Also write audit log entries for every throttle/fallback so security/compliance teams can review.

sam: Implementation detail: add route key to request context to pipeline decisions server-side. Example header: `x-redwood-route: burst` so internal routing and telemetry can tag traces. Also add API field in admin console to grant 'test' exemptions.

neha: Edge-case: integration tests and bot probes are very bursty and will drain credits. We need either 'system' tag to exempt keys or dedicated test pools. Otherwise tenants get falsely flagged as noisy.

maya: Rollout plan: feature flag 'burst-priority-v2' + gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated checks. Need a short runbook for false positives and a rollback path.

jordan: Runbook bullets: if noisy_neighbor_detection_rate > 1% AND 95th latency regresses > 20% then rollback. Also provide quick link in Console to disable feature for an org.

sam: I'll mock Console UI this afternoon. @maya can you draft tooltip text? I'll wire backend once API spec is final.

maya: Draft tooltip: 'Soft burst fallback: during short spikes we may route requests to cheaper model variants or delay responses briefly to preserve overall latency and reduce failed requests. Turning this on reduces hard rejects but may alter output quality.'

eric: One more: billing. Ensure we include fallback_model_cost in billing events so finance isn't surprised by migration to cheaper/expensive models. Add granular line items for fallback usage.

ops-bot: canary deployed to 10% orgs. observing canary metrics now...
